credentials.description: API key (Authorization: App <key>); keys have an expiry date and can be revoked
your account's base URL, https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown in the Infobip API Resource hub — it identifies the account, the key authenticates it

parameters.name: pinId
parameters.description: ID of the pin code that has to be verified.

example_prompt: Check the PIN a user typed against the Infobip 2FA pinId and only log them in when it is verified.

msisdn.description: Phone number (`MSISDN`) to which the 2FA message was sent.

pinError.description: Indicates whether an error has occurred during PIN verification.

verified.description: Indicates whether the phone number (`MSISDN`) was successfully verified.

gotchas: Send the API key as 'Authorization: App <API_KEY>' — the prefix App; Bearer is only for OAuth 2.0 access tokens. Infobip API keys have a predefined expiry date and can be revoked at any time; a missing or invalid credential answers 401.
The OpenAPI lists these API key scopes for this endpoint (x-scopes): 2fa:manage, 2fa:pin:send. Give the key a matching scope when you create it.

Each Infobip account has its own base URL, xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown once you log in to the Infobip API Resource hub. Set it in INFOBIP_BASE_URL (https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com in this spec is a placeholder). It identifies your account, the API key authenticates it.
Decide on the verified field, not on the HTTP status: the response also carries attemptsRemaining and pinError.

Attempts and verification frequency are capped by the 2FA application (pinAttempts, verifyPinLimit — 1 per 3 seconds by default). allowMultiplePinVerifications defaults to true: set it to false if a PIN must not verify twice.
Errors on this endpoint are { requestError: { serviceException: { messageId, text } } } — not the errorCode shape of the SMS v3 endpoints.
